_about: THE SAMPLE PROJECT — Dragan, a feature.
ONE sample, in ONE file. It used to be two: a four-scene 'Sample — Dragon'
seeded by the hub's first-run panel, and a separate Por Thozhil field dump
embedded in src/pages/feature.js and fetched from a root JSON file. Two
samples meant two answers to 'what does a filled studio look like', and the
short one could not fill a single downstream module.
Everything the hub seeds is here and nowhere else — invariant 2. The hub
reads this file and writes it through the same models the app reads:
src/lib/scenes.js, contacts.js, locations.js, shots.js, script.js, and the
estimator's own ci_<n>_* field shape. No second representation:
* scene ids are DERIVED from the scene number ('dragan-sc-<number>'), so
a shot, a call sheet or a frame refers to a scene by NUMBER here and
the hub resolves it once. Nothing in this file writes an id twice.
* shoot days, locations, cast and page counts are NOT listed anywhere.
They are what the scene rows already say, and the stripboard, day out
of days, calendar and budget all read them back off the scenes.
* the blueprint's own legacy tables (sl_*, cast_*, loc_*, shot_*) are
deliberately left EMPTY. Filling them would be the scene list stored a
second time, which is the stranded-key trap CLAUDE.md names.
* v2s11_days and v2s11_pages are filled by the hub FROM the scenes, not
typed here, so the paperwork cannot disagree with the schedule.
PHASES 03 AND 04 ARE EMPTY ON PURPOSE. Dragan is a film that has not shot
yet — first day 12 January 2026, draft locked, recce done, two locations
still waiting on written permission. Ticking the production and
post-production checklists would describe a shoot that has not happened,
and a sample that lies about its own state teaches the wrong thing about
what the progress numbers mean.
Dragan is invented. The names, numbers and rates are plausible Chennai
figures for a mid-budget Tamil feature, not quotes from a real production.
title: Dragan

blueprint.s1_whatif: What if the debt you have been paying for twenty years was never yours — and the proof is in a ledger the man who wrote it will never hand over?
blueprint.s1_why_me: My father paid a lorry loan he had not signed because refusing it would have meant calling a dead man a liar. Nobody in that street thought it was strange.
blueprint.s1_image: A mechanic counting the same eleven thousand rupees twice, on a bench, under an inspection lamp, before he puts it in an envelope he has folded the same way for two hundred and forty months.
blueprint.s2_log1: A Chennai mechanic discovers the loan he has been repaying for twenty years is a forgery.
blueprint.s2_log2: A mechanic who has spent twenty years paying his dead brother's debt learns the ledger was faked, and must drive one illegal consignment to get his hands on the original.
blueprint.s2_log_final: SELVAM, a Pudupet lorry mechanic everyone calls Dragan, has paid his dead brother's debt for twenty years — until his niece's college fee forces him to read the ledger properly and see that the signature is not his brother's. To get the original book out of the moneylender's almirah he agrees to drive one consignment north, and discovers the only way to stop paying is to say out loud, in front of the street, that his brother could not write.
blueprint.s3_theme: A debt you never owed is still a debt until you refuse it out loud.
blueprint.s3_ext: Can Selvam get the original ledger out of Chettiar's almirah before the fee deadline, without losing the garage or Rafi's hands?
blueprint.s3_int: Can he stop protecting his brother's name at the cost of his niece's future?
blueprint.s3_phil: Is loyalty to the dead a virtue, or the cheapest form of cowardice available to the living?
blueprint.s4_arc: A man who spent twenty years paying so nobody would ask a question, standing in the lane and answering it himself.
blueprint.s4_want: The original ledger, and the fee receipt in Kaviya's hand before the 31st.
blueprint.s4_need: To let his brother be smaller than he has been keeping him.
blueprint.s4_lie: If I keep paying, nothing else has to be said.
blueprint.s4_wound: He read the promissory note aloud at fourteen and his brother told him to stop showing off.
blueprint.s4_skill: He can hear a gearbox and name the tooth.
blueprint.s5_want: That the street keeps believing a book is the same thing as the truth.
blueprint.s5_philosophy: I did not invent the interest. I only wrote down what everybody had already agreed to.
blueprint.s5_hero: He is right that Selvam signed nothing and paid anyway. The forgery worked because Selvam wanted it to.
blueprint.s5_mirror: Both men are keeping a dead man's reputation alive — one for money, one for love, and neither for Murugan.
blueprint.s5_humanity: He pays the school fees of four boys in his lane and keeps the receipts in the same almirah.
blueprint.s6_ally_reflect: He is the fourteen-year-old Selvam was, and he can read.
blueprint.s6_ally_subplot: He is studying at night for a diploma Selvam does not know about.
blueprint.s6_ally_exit: He is the one who photographs the ledger page, and the one whose hand is broken for it.
blueprint.s6_lover_sees: That the twenty years were never for Murugan.
blueprint.s6_lover_goal: To get Kaviya out of the lane before the lane decides what she is.
blueprint.s6_lover_decision: She tells the police what her husband could and could not write.
blueprint.s6_mentor_tool: He teaches Selvam that a weighbridge slip is also a signature.
blueprint.s6_mentor_failure: He took the same kind of loan in 1996 and never fought it.
blueprint.s7_location: North Chennai — Pudupet, Sowcarpet, Vyasarpadi, Kasimedu — and the NH-16 corridor up to Nellore
blueprint.s7_duration: Nineteen days, against a fee deadline of 31 January
blueprint.s7_rules: 1. No song sequence. 2. Nobody in this film owns a car. 3. Every document on screen is legible and can be read by the audience. 4. The police are neither saviours nor villains; they are slow. 5. Violence happens off the beat, never on it.
blueprint.s7_sensory: Grease black, ledger red, sodium orange. The sound of a 12-inch impact wrench and a ceiling fan with a bent blade. Rain only once, in the last reel.
blueprint.s9_chrono: 2004 harbour → 2004 note signed → twenty years of payments (elided) → present-day fee notice → the read → the consignment → the ledger → the lane.
blueprint.s9_screen: Present-day payment first. The 2004 harbour is held back to the middle of the second act, so the audience believes the debt is real for forty minutes.
blueprint.s9_why: The film is about a document being taken on trust. The audience should take it on trust too, and feel the cost of having done so.

blueprint.s10_pay_1: Rafi reading the forged signature aloud in the office.
blueprint.s10_setup_2: Chettiar licking his thumb before turning a ledger page.
blueprint.s10_pay_2: The smudge that dates the ink.
blueprint.s10_setup_3: The bent fan blade in the office.
blueprint.s10_pay_3: The photograph is blurred because the page is moving.
blueprint.s10_setup_4: Murugan's thumbprint on the ice-lorry permit.
blueprint.s10_pay_4: The note carries a signature, not a thumbprint.
blueprint.s10_setup_5: Kaviya's fee notice hidden under the rice tin.
blueprint.s10_pay_5: The receipt pinned to the same tin in the last shot.

blueprint.s12_note_v1: The film is eleven scenes of paperwork and one chase. Do not let the chase become the point.
blueprint.v2s1_weak: 1. The middle of act two is two dhaba scenes doing one job. 2. Inspector Jeyaraman explains the law twice. 3. The canal chase is written bigger than the budget.
blueprint.v2s1_signoff: Director, producer and DOP on 24 Dec. Editor read it cold on 27 Dec and flagged the dhaba pair.
blueprint.v2s2_theme: A debt you never owed is still a debt until you refuse it out loud.
blueprint.v2s2_tone1: Procedural, unhurried, warm about people and cold about paper.
blueprint.v2s2_tone2: Patient · tactile · unsentimental · funny in the garage
blueprint.v2s2_refs: Visaranai for the procedure, Kaala for the lane as an organism, and Sudhir Patwardhan's Bombay paintings for the middle distance.
blueprint.v2s2_refuse: No song sequence. No slow-motion entry. No item of violence the audience enjoys. No montage of the twenty years. No rain until the last reel.
blueprint.v2s2_para: This is a film about a document. Everything we build — the lane, the office, the cab — exists so that when a piece of paper is held up to a bulb, the audience can read it too. If a scene cannot be shot so that the paper in it is legible, we will restage the scene rather than cut away.
blueprint.v2s3_palette: Grease black, ledger red, sodium orange
blueprint.v2s3_light: Single-source practicals in the garage. Sodium vapour on all night exteriors. Ravi Varman's daylight interiors for the hospital corridor.
blueprint.v2s3_frames: Waist-level two-shots in the lane. The office always from the visitor's chair. The cab interior only from the passenger side. Kasimedu wide at 18mm, once.
blueprint.v2s3_texture: Cotton gone grey, grease under a fingernail, ledger paper soft at the corner from twenty years of thumbs.

blueprint.v2s11_blocks: Three blocks: Chennai lane and interiors (days 1–9), the NH-16 run (days 10–12), Chennai nights and pickups (days 13–18).

blueprint.v2s12_recce: 8–10 Jan 2026 — Pudupet lane, Sowcarpet office, Vyasarpadi house, Buckingham Canal bank, Kasimedu harbour.
blueprint.v2s12_problems: 1. Pudupet lane trades until 21:00 and will not close. 2. Canal bank has no vehicle access for a genny. 3. Kasimedu dawn window is 22 minutes. 4. Sowcarpet office ceiling is 2.4m — no top light. 5. Stanley corridor permission is per-shift, not per-day.
blueprint.v2s12_resolutions: 1. Shoot lane 05:30–08:30, two days, AD Nivetha owns the traders. 2. Battery-only lighting on the canal, gaffer Jagan. 3. Two dawn days at Kasimedu, not one. 4. Bounce off a white ceiling tile, DOP Hari agreed. 5. Production exec Yuvaraj holds a shift-by-shift permission file.
blueprint.v2s12_note: Read the note aloud on the first morning. That is the whole film.
blueprint.lad_1_logline: A Pudupet mechanic who has paid his dead brother's debt for twenty years finds the ledger was forged, and has to say so in front of the street that named him.
blueprint.lad_2_synopsis: Selvam repairs lorry gearboxes in Pudupet and pays eleven thousand rupees a month to a Sowcarpet moneylender against a note his brother signed in 2004. When his niece's college fee falls due he asks to see the note, and his apprentice — who can read — tells him the signature is not a man's who used a thumbprint on every other paper he ever touched. The original book is in Chettiar's almirah, and the price of the almirah opening is one consignment driven to Nellore and back.
blueprint.lad_3_onepager: Genre: crime drama. Length: 110 pages / 36 scenes. Budget: ₹4.6 cr. Schedule: 18 days, North Chennai and NH-16. Comparable: Visaranai, Kuttrame Thandanai. The hook is a document the audience can read.
blueprint.lad_5_outline: Fifteen beats, in Vol I step 11. Act two turns on a weighbridge slip, not on a fight.

scenes.synopsis: 2004. Two brothers unload ice before first light. Murugan signs a paper he cannot read and hands it back smiling.
Present day. Selvam walks the lane. Every shutter calls him Dragan; not one of them uses his name.
Selvam and Rafi drop a gearbox. On the bench an envelope waits with this month's payment, counted twice.
Chettiar reads the ledger aloud, as he has every month for twenty years. The principal has never moved.
Mallika serves food she does not eat. Kaviya's fee notice is under the rice tin, where she thinks he will not look.
Ninety-two thousand by the 31st, says the clerk, and there is no instalment scheme for a second-year transfer.
Selvam asks Kaviya what she would do if the money did not come. She tells him, and he does not like the answer.
Dr Nirmala explains, for the second time, that Mallika's medication is not the thing that can be postponed.
Periyasamy offers Selvam a run north. He also tells him what a weighbridge slip is worth in a court.
Kaviya asks the clerk to hold her seat for nine days and signs an undertaking she has not read.
Vetri collects from four shutters before he reaches Selvam's, so the lane can watch the order of things.
Rafi corrects the bill Selvam has written. It is the first time the film shows that one of them can read and one of them cannot do it fast.
Mallika finds the fee notice where she left it and understands that he has known for four days.
Twenty-two hours of road in one cab. Selvam has not been told what is behind him, and does not ask until Gummidipoondi.
Selvam stops for a leak and reads the manifest by the light of the cab door. Two of the four items do not exist.
Vetri is waiting at the dhaba with a second driver's licence and Selvam's own name on it.

scenes.synopsis: The slip is four tonnes light. Selvam signs it, and the film records exactly what signing something you have not read looks like.

Selvam asks Mallika whether her husband could write. She says the sentence that ends the second act.
Inspector Jeyaraman explains, without unkindness, that a photograph of a page is not a document.
Sarasu has kept every trip sheet for nine years under the cash box, and lets Selvam look.

The receipt goes into Kaviya's hand and then onto the rice tin at home, where the notice used to be.

shots.description: Crane down the length of the lane, finding Selvam small in it. One take, before the shutters open.
Travel with Selvam at waist level. Every greeting comes from off-frame.
The gearbox in the gunny sack changing hands. No faces.
The shutter that calls him Dragan. Held two beats after he leaves frame.
The garage entire, one practical. Establishes where the bench is for the rest of the film.
Selvam over the gearbox, listening rather than looking.
The envelope. Eleven thousand, counted twice, and the fold.
Rafi to the calendar and back. First plant of the date.
The dhaba from the lorry's cab. Vetri is already in the frame and we do not point at him.
Push to the table as the licence comes out of the jacket.
Selvam's own name on a licence he has never held. Legible — the audience reads it with him.
Sarasu at the stove, hearing all of it and saying nothing.
The embankment from above: 5.8 metres of bank, 2.6 metres of lorry. The whole chase is in this shot.
Wheel-height track with the near-side tyre, 40cm from the edge. Second unit.
Selvam in the cab at eleven kilometres an hour, which is the fastest anybody moves in this film.
Rafi's fall, in one, from across the water. No cut into it.

elements.text: Ice, and the smell of it. Two brothers work a slab down a ramp with hooks. MURUGAN, thirty, does the pulling. YOUNG SELVAM, fourteen, does the steering.
A man in a white shirt waits at the bottom of the ramp with a paper on a clipboard. He has been waiting a while and does not mind.
Murugan wipes his hand on his lungi twice before he takes the pen. Young Selvam leans in to read the page.
Murugan puts his thumb on the ink pad. He presses it to the paper, slow and careful, the way a man does a thing he is proud of doing properly.
The man in the white shirt looks at the thumbprint. Then he takes the clipboard back.

Twenty years later, and a metre narrower. Shutters both sides, stacked to the ceiling with gearboxes, alternators, half a bus. SELVAM, forty-four, walks up the middle of it with a gunny sack on one shoulder.
Dragan! Fifty-two teeth, not fifty-four. I told you.
You told me on Thursday. It was already open on Wednesday.
Laughter down the lane. Another shutter.
Nobody in the lane uses his name. It has been so long that nobody in the lane remembers there is one.
One room, one bulb on a wandering lead, and a bench that has been in the same place since 2006. RAFI, nineteen, is under the lorry. Selvam is over the gearbox.
On the bench: an envelope. Beside it, a wall calendar, January.
Third gear is the one making the noise.
Third gear is telling you about second gear. Listen again.
Rafi listens again. Selvam picks up the envelope, opens it, and counts the notes. He counts them a second time, and folds the flap the way he has folded it two hundred and forty times.
Anna. How much is left on it?
Selvam puts the envelope in his shirt pocket.

documents.title: Dragan — treatment, draft 4
documents.body:
A man pays a debt for twenty years because reading it would mean calling his dead brother a liar.

SELVAM repairs lorry gearboxes in a Pudupet lane where nobody uses his name. On the first of every month he counts eleven thousand rupees into an envelope and carries it to ANBU CHETTIAR in Sowcarpet, against a promissory note his brother MURUGAN signed at the Kasimedu ice ramp in 2004. The principal has never moved. Selvam has never asked it to.

His niece KAVIYA needs ninety-two thousand rupees by the thirty-first. There is no instalment scheme for a second-year transfer. For the first time in twenty years Selvam asks to hold the note, and Chettiar — who has not been asked twice in two decades — lets him.

RAFI, nineteen, reads it for him. The signature is a signature. Murugan put his thumb on every paper he ever touched, because a thumb was what he had.

What follows is not a revenge film. A photograph of a page is not a document, as INSPECTOR JEYARAMAN explains on the Marina without any unkindness at all; the original book is in an almirah, and the price of the almirah opening is one consignment driven to Nellore and back with a manifest that lists two things which do not exist. Selvam drives it. He signs a weighbridge slip four tonnes light, and in signing it he does the exact thing he is trying to undo.

The almirah opens in the third act and the ledger is not in it. It is on a canal bank in Vyasarpadi, where a frightened man threw it, and getting to it costs Rafi the use of a hand for four months.

The film ends with the smallest possible act. Selvam stands in the lane at six in the morning and reads the note out loud — all of it, including the part that says his brother could not write his own name. MALLIKA stands next to him while he does it. The receipt goes on the rice tin where the fee notice used to be.

110 pages. 36 scenes. 18 days. No song sequence.

documents.title: Director's statement
documents.body:
I grew up in a street where at least four families were paying something they had not signed. Nobody thought this was strange, and nobody thought it was a story either, because the whole thing is paperwork and paperwork is supposed to be boring.

So the discipline of this film is that every document on screen is legible. If a page is held up to a bulb, the audience reads it at the same moment the character does. That one rule decides the lenses (a 100mm macro is on the truck every day), the lighting (practicals first, warm shadows, nothing crushed), and the blocking (the office is always shot from the visitor's chair).

There is one chase, and it happens at eleven kilometres an hour on an embankment three metres wider than the vehicle on it. It is the most frightening thing in the film precisely because nothing in it is fast.

What I do not want: a montage of the twenty years, a slow-motion entry, or a single frame of violence the audience enjoys. What I do want is for somebody to leave the theatre and go home and read something they have been paying.

documents.title: One-pager — for the market
documents.body:
DRAGAN
Crime drama · Tamil · 110 pages · 18 shoot days · ₹4.6 cr

LOGLINE
A Pudupet mechanic who has paid his dead brother's debt for twenty years finds the ledger was forged, and has to say so in front of the street that named him.

WHY NOW
India is a country of documents people cannot read and payments they cannot stop. The film is small, specific and has no villain who is wrong.

COMPARABLES
Visaranai (2015) · Kuttrame Thandanai (2016) · Jai Bhim (2021) for the procedural spine.

PACKAGE
Director Arunkumar A · DOP Hari Shankar · Editor Praveen Antony · PD Meera Raghavan · Producer Bhuvana Sekar, Red Ice Pictures.

STATUS
Draft 4 locked 22 Dec 2025. Recce complete. Floor from 12 Jan 2026. Two locations pending written permission.

documents.title: Character bible — Selvam
documents.body:
SELVAM, 44. Called Dragan since 2006, after a dragon on a lorry mudflap he rebuilt; the name stuck because it was easier than his.

WANT: the original ledger, and the fee receipt in Kaviya's hand before the 31st.
NEED: to let his brother be smaller than he has been keeping him.
LIE: if I keep paying, nothing else has to be said.
WOUND: he read the note aloud at fourteen and was told to stop showing off. He has not read anything aloud since.
SKILL: he can hear a gearbox and name the tooth.
FLAW: he mistakes silence for protection.

HOW HE CHANGES: nothing external forces the last scene. No police officer needs it, no court requires it, and Kaviya's fee is already paid. He reads the note out loud in the lane because the only way to stop paying a debt you never owed is to say out loud that you never owed it.
